significance: A field of small grey coral-stone stupas at Kantharodai in the Jaffna peninsula, the most striking Buddhist archaeological site in northern Sri Lanka. Its history reaches back to the Anuradhapura era, a stone pillar there dates to the reign of Dappula IV, Polonnaruwa-period coins have been recovered, and finds include fragments of Buddha and Bodhisattva statues and Buddha footprint slabs.
story: The little stupas are said to hold the remains of sixty arhat monks who died together at the site, by poisoned mushroom curry or by famine, while fleeing persecution.
